mistakes.title: Forgetting the quotes around text
mistakes.explanation: Beginners assume print(Hello) works because it reads naturally.
mistakes.traceback:
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<stdin>", line 1, in <module>
NameError: name 'Hello' is not defined
mistakes.fix: Wrap text in quotes so Python knows it is text, not a variable name.

mistakes.title: Using a single equal sign for comparison
mistakes.explanation: Beginners often confuse assignment with comparison, thinking a single equals sign checks equality.
mistakes.traceback:
File "<stdin>", line 2
    if x = 10:
       ^^^^^^
SyntaxError: invalid syntax. Maybe you meant '==' or ':=' instead of '='?
mistakes.fix: Use double equals (==) for comparison to check if two values are equal.

mistakes.title: Missing parentheses in print function
mistakes.explanation: Beginners may forget that print is a function and not a statement, leading them to omit the parentheses.
mistakes.traceback:
File "<stdin>", line 1
    print "Hello, world!"
    ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
SyntaxError: Missing parentheses in call to 'print'. Did you mean print(...)?
mistakes.fix: Always include parentheses when using print to ensure it is treated as a function call.
